title: Facial Pain

rationale.Physical Exam: Facial sensation: Allodynia in V1 distribution. Prior vesicular rash scars.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with persistent, severe, burning/shooting pain in the trigeminal nerve distribution (V1 most common) following a recent herpes zoster (shingles) outbreak with characteristic vesicular rash in the same distribution. Postherpetic neuralgia is the most common complication of HZ — pain persisting >90 days after rash resolution. Risk increases with age (>60). Caused by viral damage to sensory ganglia → neuropathic pain. Treatment: first-line — gabapentin or pregabalin, TCAs (amitriptyline, nortriptyline), lidocaine patch 5% (localized pain). Opioids NOT first-line. Prevention: recombinant zoster vaccine (Shingrix) for adults ≥50 — reduces HZ risk by >90% and PHN risk. VZV is reactivation of latent varicella virus in dorsal root ganglia.
